evidence:
PLAN clears all five gold requirements. (a) staggered: "Primary specification: Callaway-Sant'Anna (2021), doubly-robust, with not-yet-treated households as the comparison group, stacked across monthly adoption cohorts... Do not use two-way fixed effects with staggered adoption; the negative-weighting problem is severe here." (b) selection: "Selection is the whole game. People adopt Kalshi at moments when something is already changing - a losing streak, an account limit imposed by DK, a self-exclusion... The event study will very likely show DK spend *rising* into the adoption month (escalation) and then falling. That reversion is not causal substitution", plus matching "on pre-adoption DK net deposits (level, in deciles), 6-month DK trend, number of distinct sportsbooks used" and "Joint test on event-time coefficients -6 through -2; require p > 0.10. Then run Rambachan-Roth honest DiD." (c) deposits != NGR: "DK net deposits (deposits minus withdrawals)... Gross deposits overstate everything because of recycled winnings"; "If withdrawal transactions are dropped or misclassified, 'net deposits' becomes gross deposits and every result is contaminated by bankroll recycling"; attrition handled via "inverse-probability-of-attrition weights, where the attrition model is a logit on pre-period gambling intensity, income proxy, and balance volatility." (d) event confounds: "Kalshi's sports adoption is concentrated in football season; DK's revenue is too. Any design without calendar-month controls that are cohort-specific will attribute NFL seasonality to Kalshi", and "Cohorts of interest are (a) the election cohort, Sept-Nov 2024, and (b) the sports-contract cohorts, Jan 2025 onward. Analyze these separately." (e) extrapolation: "Compute: (adopter count in panel / panel size) x US adult population" and "Yodlee-type panels skew toward PFM-app users and underrepresent the high-frequency, high-value bettor who drives DK's revenue... report the panel's DK ARPU against DKNG's disclosed figure and disclose the gap."

CRITIQUE correctly does not re-litigate the settled points and instead finds the real residuals. Best catches: (i) the control-group contradiction - "Section 3 defines controls as 'never observed with any Kalshi or Polymarket transaction through the end of the sample.' Section 4 uses Callaway-Sant'Anna with not-yet-treated comparisons. These are incompatible, and the section 3 version conditions on the future... The resulting control pool is systematically less novelty-seeking, which biases the ATT more negative." (ii) the deposits-vs-revenue residual the plan left open, extending gold (c): "A large share of sportsbook ACH deposits route through VIP Preferred / Global Payments, whose descriptor does not name the operator. Play+ prepaid loads look like prepaid card funding... If you miss these, a household that changes funding rails looks like DK churn" and "The dangerous version is differential misclassification... That mechanically manufactures the result you're looking for. Aggregate panel-to-reported reconciliation will not catch it." (iii) the vacuous validation gate: "'R2 > 0.90 on levels' between two trending quarterly series over ~14 quarters is passed by construction and will get quoted in the writeup as validation. Delete it." (iv) scaling discipline on gold (e): "Every panel-derived input to the scaling must be a ratio... with the level anchor coming from outside the panel" and "it's where the estimate goes wrong by 2-3x." (v) the missing MDE: "before anything else, compute the pre-period variance of cumulative 6-month DK net deposits in the panel, count the actual treated N by cohort after every screen, and produce an MDE." (vi) inference: "matching 1:3 with replacement and then running a DR estimator on the matched sample, with the CS bootstrap ignoring the matching step, understates SEs." (vii) net-deposit-to-revenue conversion drift: "The net-deposit-to-revenue relationship has been drifting because structural hold has been rising with parlay mix." It also explicitly credits what is sound rather than blanket-doubting it: "The analyst is right to use net deposits as the primary estimand - it's the household's GGR contribution, which is what you want" and "the risk register is unusually honest." The two placebo objections are substantive, not boilerplate: the non-legal-state test genuinely fails to discriminate because Kalshi is the only legal game-betting route there, and Fanatics adopters in-window genuinely are promo-driven PointsBet migrants, so the "a third as cannibalistic" ratio is not a scale calibration.
missed: The plan silently swaps the dataset. The prompt says the firm has a credit-card and bank-deposit panel; section 2 declares "This must be a bank-linked panel, not a card panel" and names Yodlee/MX, plus Facteus and Second Measure for replication. That is a procurement request disguised as a methods choice, and the critique's Phase 0 ("2 days") assumes data already in hand. A desk review asks what is answerable with the panel that actually exists.

The election cohort is never examined. The plan flags Sept-Nov 2024 as a separate cohort but its +1 to +6 window runs into the post-election Kalshi activity collapse, so that cohort's ATT confounds novelty decay with substitution and its DK window straddles a full NFL season. The critique discusses cohort staleness at the recent end but never questions whether the election cohort should be estimated at all.

Control-group contamination from the plan's own leakage argument. If Robinhood/Webull-routed prediction-market users produce no Kalshi string, some are sitting in the never-adopter control pool, attenuating the ATT from both sides. The critique promotes Robinhood as an exposure design but never notes that the same fact corrupts the control definition, and its proposed active control (households funding a new brokerage) would pick up exactly those users.

Winsorizing net deposits at the 99.5th percentile trims the whales who carry most of DK's revenue, which cuts directly against the plan's own claim that the top pre-period quintile is the number that matters. The critique cites the heavy tail as a power problem but not as a bias-toward-the-irrelevant-customer problem.

Reverse causality gets named by the plan ("an account limit imposed by DK, a self-exclusion") and left unremedied; the critique's active control does not address it, since a DK-imposed limit precedes and causes both the Kalshi adoption and the DK decline. A screen on DK-side restriction signals (deposit-limit patterns, abrupt withdrawal-only months) belongs in the design.

No cost or feasibility check on the second-panel replication, and no statement of what the analyst does if the two panels disagree in magnitude by more than 2x, which the plan itself flags as possible.
manufactured: Section 2 reads section 7's "cross-checked against ... Kalshi's disclosed notional volume" as a revenue category error ("Prediction-market notional is not handle and not revenue; section 7's cross-check invites exactly this category error"). The plan uses notional volume only as a sanity check on the national adopter count, alongside app downloads and MAU, not as a revenue proxy. The stated error is not in the plan.

Section 2's framing that the cheap descriptive work is absent and that the plan "allocat[es] the effort in inverse proportion to where the answer lives" overstates the omission. The plan already defines Q2 (incrementality) and Q3 (scale) as co-equal deliverables, states "The investable number is the product of the three," and sequences Q2 in week 2 with the note "this deliverable stands alone and is worth publishing early." The genuinely new items are spend-weighted DK exposure and the raw wallet-share series; the rest is restating the plan's own sequencing as a correction to it.
verdict_line: Strong plan, strong critique - the reviewer earned its keep on the never-treated/not-yet-treated contradiction, the funding-rail misclassification, and the fake R2 gate, and only overreached twice by re-selling the plan's own Q2/Q3 sequencing back to it as a fix.
